---
title: "FAQ & Troubleshooting"
description: "Common problems when preparing input files and running INTEGRATOR, and how to resolve them."
---

This page collects frequent questions and failure modes. For the input-file reference see
[Input Files](input-files.qmd), for choosing parameter values see
[Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd), and for the processing steps see
[Running INTEGRATOR](running.qmd).

## Preparing the input files

### A CSV file is misread — columns look shifted or values are wrong

`run_order.csv` and `feature_list.csv` are read **by column position, not by header name**, so a
reordered, deleted, or inserted column is silently misinterpreted. Restore the template column order
(see [Input Files](input-files.qmd#column-order-warning)). Beyond column order, `run_order.csv` and
`feature_list.csv` are plain, comma-separated, UTF-8 files that spreadsheet editors corrupt silently:

- **Auto-conversion** — leading zeros are dropped and values such as `16:0` or `1-2` are coerced to
  dates or times. Format the affected cells as text, or edit in a plain-text editor.
- **Delimiter / locale** — the separator must be a comma. Locales that default to a semicolon (`;`)
  produce a single-column file that is misread.
- **Encoding** — save as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark (BOM); a BOM corrupts the first header.
- **Stray whitespace and blank rows** — trailing spaces in identifiers and empty trailing rows are
  read as data.
- **File names** — the `file name` entries must match the mzML files exactly, including the `.mzML`
  extension and case.

### Which input files are required, and can they be renamed?

`param.txt` must be named `param.txt` and reside in the same folder as the executable. The sample list
and transition/feature list may take any name, set by `batch_info` and `transition_list` in
`param.txt` (defaults `run_order.csv` and `feature_list.csv`). See [Input Files](input-files.qmd).

## Validation and matching (Step 1)

### What do `missing_files.txt`, `missing_compounds.txt`, and `missing_details.txt` mean?

These are written by **Step 1 (Data Validation)** only when problems are found:

- **`missing_files.txt`** — mzML files listed in the sample list but absent from the data folder, or
  present in the folder but not listed.
- **`missing_compounds.txt`** — transitions defined in the transition list but not matched in the
  mzML files.
- **`missing_details.txt`** — which samples lack a given transition (useful when a transition is
  present in only some files).

The analysis may proceed with items missing. See
[Running INTEGRATOR — Step 1](running.qmd#step-1-data-validation).

### A transition is not matched

Matching is by precursor *m/z*, product *m/z*, and RT, within `mz_tol` and `RT_tol`. Confirm the
transition-list values against the mzML, and widen `mz_tol` if the instrument's *m/z* calibration is
slightly off.

### Why was a transition dropped from every sample?

**Current limitation.** INTEGRATOR integrates only the transitions **common to all mzML files** (their
intersection) *and* listed in the transition/feature file. A transition missing from even one mzML file
is dropped for the **whole** dataset — not only for the files that lack it — and reported in
`missing_compounds.txt` / `missing_details.txt`. Ensure the transition is acquired in every sample, or
exclude the files/features that do not share it. See
[Running INTEGRATOR — Step 1](running.qmd#step-1-data-validation).

### The same transition appears more than once in an mzML file

Where a transition with identical (or near-identical) Q1/Q3 and MRM windows occurs multiple times,
INTEGRATOR prompts for which MRM index to map to the feature; the `chromatogram index` column in the
transition list can also fix the assignment.

## Peak detection and integration

### A feature's area is reported as zero

No peak was detected within `RT_tol` of the expected RT. Check the expected `RT` in the transition
list, confirm the precursor/product *m/z* match within `mz_tol`, and, for genuinely drifting peaks,
widen `RT_tol`. See [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### A wrong, co-eluting, or adjacent peak is integrated

Usually `RT_tol` or `peak_width` is too wide, or the expected RT is off. Narrow the window, or set a
per-feature `peak width` or fixed integration bounds for the affected feature. Confirm every change in
[MRMhub-viz](viz.qmd) before re-integrating. See [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### Retention-time drift is not tracked across the sequence

Reference samples must be chosen from **early** in the sequence and be mutually well aligned, and
`RT_shift` / `RT_shift_bound` must accommodate the real drift. See
[Peak-detection algorithm](algorithm.qmd) and [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### I edited an input file — what must be re-run?

Editing any input file requires restarting from **Step 1**. Editing only `RT_matrix.csv` (manual
border adjustments) requires re-running **Step 3** alone — re-running Step 2 overwrites `RT_matrix.csv`.
See [Running INTEGRATOR](running.qmd).

## Running the application

### The application will not open (macOS "cannot be verified" / Windows "blocked")

The executables are unsigned, so the operating system shows a one-time security prompt on first
launch. See [clearing the first-launch security prompt](setup.qmd#clearing-the-first-launch-security-prompt).
